# Recreation Prompt

Create a portrait-first browser-native canvas board game titled `Final Call: Rulebreaker`. Preserve a Ludo-like four-player dice race: players take turns tapping a phone/die button, roll 1-6, move along a shared 40-step loop, enter a 5-step home/final-act path, must land exactly on step 44 to win, and send opponents back to start when they land on the same shared track tile outside safe zones. Present the world as a Scream-style meta-horror mystery with Ghostface-like mask silhouettes, self-aware slasher rule jokes, phone-call UI, teen suspect tokens, evidence strings, VHS grain, and mobile-readable portrait controls. Use inline HTML/CSS/JS and procedural Canvas/CSS art rather than relying on local media assets.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source Game Truth
- genre: turn-based Ludo-like canvas board race
- objective: each of four players taps a die, advances around a shared 40-tile loop and 5-tile home path, and wins by reaching step 44 exactly
- input model: native click/tap buttons for start, die roll, and restart; no keyboard or drag requirement
- core loop: current player rolls 1-6, animates step-by-step movement, checks exact-finish, checks collisions, then advances turn
- fail/friction state: over-roll stalls the current turn; collisions on shared non-safe track tiles reset the bumped player to step 0

## Protected Mechanics
- Four-player cyclic turn order, including finished-player skip behavior.
- Random six-sided die and visible roll animation.
- Step-by-step movement timing and board position model.
- Same absolute-track collision reset outside start and home safe zones.
- Exact finish at step 44 and restart to all pieces at step 0.

## Safe Transformation Surfaces
HUD vocabulary, title, player names, colors, background, board tile rendering, token silhouettes, feedback copy, fonts, audio labels, and ambient procedural art are safe to transform because they do not alter the rules.
